claims.claim: A character randomly appears during a night to add an extra animatronic to the mix unexpectedly.

citations.review_text: For the 7th official game in the Series, It is alright, It feels more like a Bonus thing or a Spin-Off than an actual Game Itself weirdly? I couldn't personally get into it, and It feels very overwhelming with the controls, but It does have Its charm. I mean the Combinations are cool, and the Lore I guess is unique, but It's more of a Challenge Game than anything. If you are playing this expecting Story, or even 5 nights like the previous games, you aren't getting that, It's a Custom Match Maker for your favorite Animatronics. Though, my biggest thing about this Game is that randomly throughout a Night, a little gremlin appears and just adds a Random Character to the Mix that you probably don't even know how to defend against, which seems more punishing than anything. If you are playing casually, I don't recommend, but If you are looking for a Challenge, then this is for you. Overall I'd give it a 6.5/10.

Imagine learning Mr. Hippo tells a story every time he jumpscares you. So you start the game, put Mr. Hippo to 20 and wait, while you are waiting you hear "HOW UNFORTUNATE! UH OH HOW UNFORTUNATE! UH OH I KNOW HOW MUCH YOU LIKE TO FIGHT SO ILL ADD A NEW PROBLEM TO YOUR NIGHT" Everything does quiet the lights turn off, you know its not Mr. Hippo and rage quit. This was my experience one time other than that great game, play it Dee Dee is annoying as heck tho, unless you're doing Dee Dee roulette.

claims.claim: Players can customize matches by selecting individual animatronics and adjusting their difficulty levels.

citations.review_text: I like it. Have all the animatronics try to kill you is cool. And they don't just attack you, you have to manage power, learn how to deal with the animatronics, deal with the animatronics. And if you can't handle 50/20, you can choose who you want attacking you.

Ultimate Custom Night puts fifty animatronics from across the series into one game, and lets you build your own night by picking who shows up and setting their difficulty from 0 to 20, all for free. I've played the older FNAF games and liked them, so I figured this one would be right up my alley too, but it just never clicked for me. The older games got me with that slow, creepy build-up, the feeling of something getting closer while you're too scared to check the cameras. UCN doesn't really have that. Instead you're staring at a screen full of doors, vents, and buttons, trying to keep track of way too much at once. It didn't feel scary, it just felt like a lot of noise, and I ended up putting it down pretty quickly. I get why people who like a tough challenge are into it, there's clearly a ton packed into this game, it just wasn't for me.

claims.claim: Reviewers highlight the large roster of customizable animatronics included in the game.

citations.review_text:
I thought Ultimate Custom Night was just another FNAF game where you survive against a bunch of animatronics.

I was wrong.

The graphics aren't anything revolutionary. The gameplay sounds simple: sit in an office, watch cameras, close doors, check vents, and try not to die.

Then you realize there are **50 animatronics** trying to kill you.

And somehow, it works.

Every animatronic has its own behavior, its own rules, and its own way of making your life miserable. You think you've finally figured everything out, and then one tiny mistake sends you straight back to the beginning.

What I love most is the customization. You decide exactly which animatronics you're dealing with and how difficult the night will be. Want a manageable challenge? You can do that.

Want absolute suffering?

You can do that too.

The sound design is incredible, especially when you're trying to keep track of everything happening around you. You're constantly listening, checking cameras, watching timers, and praying you didn't forget something.

I've played horror games with bigger worlds, better graphics, and more elaborate stories.

I don't remember most of them.

I'll remember Ultimate Custom Night.

Some games are scary because you don't know what's coming.

UCN is scary because you know **exactly** what's coming—and you still can't stop it.

100% recommended.

it is very fun and combines almost all of the aspects from most of the games, there are 50 characters that make the game feel very full of to many things, the only bad thing is that there aren't all the characters and when a new game comes out they don't get added but its still fine because there are still 50 very customizable characters
The possibility's are nearly endless and it is so fun to experience all the animatronics
This game is a lot of fun, offering an experience where you can take on challenges or experiment with all the animatronics featured in the game.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game combines mechanics and characters from across the franchise.

citations.review_text: Ultimate Custom Night is a perfect culmination of every character and game mechanic in Scott Cawthon's prior games in the franchise. While lacking on the scary side compared to Scott's usual work, the gameplay of UCN is fun, snappy, and perfect for people who like a challenge. Learning how each animatronic functions in the game is like putting the puzzle pieces together to slowly develop your own understanding and strategies for the game, eventually taking on every animatronic at once as the final task. Even in 2026, I still love this game with all my heart. Just now, I beat 50/20 for the second time (this time without using any powers) and as stressful as it was, the satisfaction of completing the night was absolutely thrilling. Although this game isn't as relevant as it once was, I would still suggest that every gamer dying for a good challenge should give this game a try.

it is very fun and combines almost all of the aspects from most of the games, there are 50 characters that make the game feel very full of to many things, the only bad thing is that there aren't all the characters and when a new game comes out they don't get added but its still fine because there are still 50 very customizable characters
I had a lot of fun with this game, it was really cool to see the elements of the games I played before crammed up into this one. This game is worth every horror fans time.

citations.review_text: Probably the best fnaf gameplay wise and it's free

[h2]Unnecessarily Complicated Ultimate Custom Night Review[/h2]

[b]TL;DR:[/b] As the name suggests, the game no longer focuses on the horror aspect but rather on the challenge of all custom nights from previous games combined. Not scary but really, really interesting to bruteforce your way through the challenges. Overall Score: 80/100 - Comfortably Recommend.

[h3]Unnecessarily Long Version with 5 Categories.[/h3]

[b]Cost per Hour:[/b] Once again - it is free ($0/h)! I don't know why the generosity but a good, free game is always appreciated. My playtime (20.1 hours) includes: all in-game challenges (some of them completed twice), some practice, [spoiler]40/20 completion, and 45/20 attempts[/spoiler]. Category Score: 10/10

[b]Gameplay:[/b] You get 50 animatronics with a lot of different mechanics. Similar to FNaF 2, some of the animatronics follow the same patterns. During your initial playthrough you will have a hard time adjusting but after a few guides on specific challenges, you will learn several crucial mechanics and the gameplay loop becomes repetitive. Almost all challenges can be beaten with just one strategy. Category Score: 6/10

[b]Visuals:[/b] So, the visuals are basically the same as every other game in the series. However, jump scares got a massive downgrade in my opinion. I understand why but I think it is just a little [i]too[/i] lazy. Still, we got a lot of cameras, different offices and characters. [spoiler]Intermissions[/spoiler] are also well-made. Category Score: 7/10

[b]Sound design:[/b] Can't say the sounds are bad, it just shows that this game is challenge-based rather than horror. The music is cool though, especially the high-score one. Category Score: 8/10

[b]Technical performance / Compatibility:[/b] The performance on Linux should be perfectly fine on any semi-modern piece of hardware. However, it is advised to disable visual effects, especially when playing on Linux. You really want to disable them anyway, regardless …

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game includes multiple different offices to unlock and a large roster of animatronics with distinct mechanics drawn from previous titles.

citations.review_text:
Ultimate Custom Night is what many fans of the series consider to be the final installation of the "original" FNaF games. It's the last game in the franchise that features the tradtional point and click gameplay, and the last one made by Scott Cawthon-the man that created FNaF. Intended to be something like a final tribute to the community from Cawthon, Ultimate Custom Night is the last(and hardest challenge) the click team era has to offer.
The name of the game is a bit self explanatory-in Ultimate Custom Night you have a rooster of 50 animatronics from all the FNaF games and you choose which ones to include and how aggressive they will be on a scale of 1 to 20 to customise your own challenges. The goal is simple-deffend yourself against the animatronics and survive until 6 a.m. 
The game is really difficult, as it combines gimmicks and mechsnics from all the FNaF games, as well as some new ones. It features different offices to unlock through reaching new high scores, power ups to help you tbrough the night and plenty of challenge presets.  There are also hidden secrets and easter eggs that give closure to a lot of the lore. Aside of the endless combinations of animatronics and difficulties, there id the ultimate challenge of 50/20, where all thrle animatronics are set on max difficulty. It's the hardest challenge in all of the FNaF games and perhaps one of the hardest in all of gaming as a whole.
Such a unique FNaF experience is not to be missed. I recommend the game to everyone-it's amazing!

A worthy conclusion to the "Clickteam" era of FNAF. Mixing and matching the dozens of different characters to create a challenge is very fun, and you get to pick and choose from nearly every single mechanic in the series. The animatronics also have quirky voice lines which gives them a lot of personality. If you enjoyed playing the previous games, you should play this one, too.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that the highest 50/20 difficulty mode is extremely difficult and punishing.

citations.review_text:
This has been one of the most enjoyable experiences I've had learning a hard game like this. It's just really satisfying and really fun being able to handle everything going on at the same time, there's not all that much downtime in this like there is in every other FNAF game and it is so incredibly satisfying. There is some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ but it's otherwise very good. 

I beat 50/20 mode and it, unlike the rest of the game, was genuinely miserable, easily the worst experience I've had playing a video game, primarily because I just got screwed over by bad luck constantly but there was some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ too. 

1. The cameras go completely static when a blackout begins and the cameras move so it's really hard to find stuff like the deathcoin.
2. Minireenas block the foxy/bonnie figurine and you have to dogde Nightmarrionne to see it.
3. Speaking of Nightmarrionne, he deserves a whole point to himself
4. Nightmarrionne, nevermind, he deserves two.
5. Why does pressing the same system button deactivate the system, 6 is already there for that reason and it can be super hard to know if a system is on sometimes, caused me to blackout past final flip in 50/20 because I thought GMC was on.
6. Rockstar is really hard to deal with no matter what difficulty you're on. He's insane.
7. 50/20 is so BUUUUUUUUUUUNS
8. Old friends is the hardest challenge, not Chaos 3

Anyway, I enjoyed the overall experience if you subject 800 points or more from the maximum score counter. My advice to people looking to go for 50/20, 50/20 is so so SOOOOO much harder than 49/20 so if you beat that fast, DO NOT underestimate 50/20. 

With this I have now 100%ed all FNAF games and can now go to bed.
Great game, plus easily the hardest of the mainline FNAF games. 50/20 was incredibly annoying, over 10 deaths past 4:00, but ultimately was a cool experience. Good game

claims.claim: Reviewers mention encountering rare bugs and freeze frame jumpscares.

citations.review_text:
I'm bored so I'm reviewing every fnaf game

It truely is amazing what Ultimate Custom Night conveyed. While it was just a case of giving the original fnaf series an epilogue, finishing with a high note, there are a lot of things in this game that I am not happy with. While I do understand the limitations of Clickteam, that makes it harder for me to enjoy the game with certain bugs (while rare) and freeze frame jumpscares. This game however, I would love to know what was going on in Scott Cawthon's head when he was writing the cinematics for Toy Chica: The Highschool Years, and Bear of Vengeance.

I'll admit I've been a FNAF fan since I was little and played the original first 4 games on my Kindle Fire, so this may be a teeny bit biased. But oh brother this guy... hands down created my absolute fav FNAF game.

It's quite literally the multiverse of FNAF characters from what could arguably be the golden era of the series, all mashed up into one extremely fun and very challenging FNAF game. It presents all the best hallmarks of a classic FNAF experience with chilling music, eerie sound effects, classic jumpscares, minigames, secret characters, secret cutscenes, etc... Oh and let's not forget the secret ending implying some BIG ol' looooooooooore...

After looking at where the series has gone, and how we compare the origins of the FNAF lore to what it has come to now, Scott Cawthon was thinking multiversal, and probably thought something along the lines of "What if I created the all in one FNAF game myself? And what if I made it the most difficult? And what if I spice it up with even MORE lore?" And he absolutely nailed it. I honestly thought it was a fan made game when I first heard about it. But when I found out Scott himself made it, that's when I knew he was thinking ahead of the game and he outdid himself literally. Very humorous how he releases a game with a maximum difficulty he can't even beat, but he knows his community is crazy enough to beat it at some point anyways...and they did LOL. And you can argue it's not as story driven or lore heavy as the first 4 games, and that's a fair point I'd agree to. But rather than a linear narrative where you're mostly listening to Phone Guy (with the exception of FNAF 4 and a few others), you interpret the hidden lore through the context of the original games themselves, and you fill in the gaps with UCN, and fairly similar to how you would fit Fazbear's Pizzeria Simulator, etc. in the overarching lore. Except this time... it's a classic FNAF experience but MUCH more amplified.

For me personally, it sits just abov…
